la:verb:coinquino.gloss: to defile, pollute or contaminate all over
senses: to defile, pollute or contaminate all over
la:verb:coinquino.html:
cŏ-inquĭno (or contr. cōnquĭno, cf. Lachm. ad ), āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.,
to defile all over, to pollute wholly, to contaminate.
Prop. (rare; not in Cic.): stercore conquinatae,; . —
Trop. *
Of infectious disease, to infect, taint: totam progeniem,.—More freq.,
Of vices: matres coinquinari regias, Att. ap. : se crimine stupri,: se maximo scelere,: cor vitiis,: famam alicujus,.— Hence, cŏinquĭnātus, a, um, P. a., polluted, contaminated: quid esse his potest coinquinatius?.

la:noun:coix.html:
cŏix, ĭcis, f., = κόϊξ,
a kind of Ethiopian palm, (Jan. coecas).

la:noun:coitio.html:
cŏĭtĭo, ōnis, f.
coëo
. *
A coming or meeting together, a meeting: prima coitio est acerrima,.—
Esp.
A uniting, banding together.
In gen. (rare): societatis,.—
In partic., in a bad sense, a conspiracy, plot, coalition (several times in Cic. and Liv.; elsewh. rare): suspitio coitionis,; : non factionibus modo nec per coitiones usitatas nobilibus, etc.,; cf. ; : candidatorum consularium,: Memmii, (15), 4: tribunorum,: facere,; : dirimere,.—
